Moore's own 2026 campaign site describes him as "the single most conservative legislator in the State of Georgia" and "100% Pro Trump"; his 2020 survey cited an American Conservative Union ranking as the seventh most conservative Georgia legislator (2019) and billed him as the "#1 Most Pro-Gun Legislator in Georgia." He was suspended indefinitely from the Senate Republican Caucus in September 2023.
COLTON MOORE.record: In the House (2019-21) he was one of ten Republicans who called for Speaker David Ralston to resign over allegations Ralston used legislative privilege to delay clients' court cases. In the Senate he was suspended indefinitely from the Republican Caucus in September 2023 after attacking colleagues who would not back his call for a special session against Fani Willis; months later Senate Republicans created a special panel to investigate Willis and Moore said "I told you so." In March 2024 he cast the lone vote against naming a University of North Georgia building for the late Ralston, calling him "one of the most corrupt Georgia leaders we'll ever see in our lifetimes"; Speaker Jon Burns barred him from the House chamber, and on January 16, 2025 he was arrested and charged with obstruction after trying to enter the House chamber despite the ban. The AJC reported that few of his bills (income-tax cuts, Second Amendment protections, COVID-19 origins) received a hearing, that he spread false claims of "secret trafficking" at Hartsfield-Jackson airport in February 2024, and that he voted against an anti-trafficking measure and opposed a deepfake bill. WILLIAM BILL OLIVER.background: William Ray "Bill" Oliver, Mountain Judicial Circuit (Habersham, Rabun and Stephens counties) Superior Court judge, appointed by Gov. Brian Kemp in December 2022 to the circuit's third judgeship created by Senate Bill 395 (2022), effective Jan. 1, 2023; elected unopposed in May 2024. Attended Gainesville College and the University of Georgia; J.D., Western Carolina University School of Law; admitted to the State Bar in 1981. Practiced at Oliver & Oliver, then co-founded Oliver & Weidner, LLC (2006); former Habersham County magistrate; appointed Habersham County Solicitor-General by Gov. Sonny Perdue in 2011; former president of the Mountain Judicial Bar Association; member of the Georgia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and Georgia Trial Lawyers Association; certified as lead counsel in death-penalty cases.
WILLIAM BILL OLIVER.notes: The governor's page metadata says Jan. 1, 2022 but body says Jan. 1, 2023 (release dated Dec. 6, 2022). Release says the vacancy was 'created by the passage of Senate Bill 395'. Local outlets (AccessWDUN, Now Habersham) call him 'Billy'.
